title: Saffy and the Sleepy Song
markdown:
Saffy had eyes as soft as the sky when it is almost night, and her little legs were still a bit wobbly, just as little legs can be. She lived in a meadow that felt like a wide warm hug. Moonbeams liked to play there. They slipped over the clover and whispered along the sleepy flowers until even the grass seemed to lean in and listen. The air smelled of sweet clover and cool evening, and the whole meadow hummed as softly as a held breath.

One night Saffy was in her little bed of clover, all snuggled and warm, when a feather-light worry tickled her nose. She could not remember a very special lullaby. It was a warm sleepy tune. It made her eyelids feel heavy and her dreams feel sweet. It always made her feel safe and sound.

Saffy’s ears drooped a tiny bit. She thought the song had wandered off without her.

Just then a soft light glowed near her nose. It was Moth, a little lantern moth whose wings held moonlight the way a leaf holds dew. She moved with a gentle flutter. Her light was not a bright startling shine. It was like a tiny friendly star that had come to visit, and it hovered as if it were asking a quiet question.

“Hello, Moth,” Saffy whispered. Her voice was as soft as leaves in a summer breeze. “I have forgotten my lullaby. The one that hums me to sleep.”

Moth’s light warmed, as if she understood. She drifted a little way into the moonlit garden, and her glow showed the path. Saffy’s wobbly legs felt steadier in the cool air. She followed. The moon made everything silver and soft blue. The garden looked like a peaceful dream. The flowers slept under moonlight blankets.

They tiptoed past the tall reeds by the pond. The reeds swayed like dancers and whispered as they moved. Cool water smelled of moss and moon. Saffy listened very closely. Their rustling sounded like soft voices. She waited, hoping the sleepy tune would rise from the pond. But it was not her lullaby.

Saffy let out a little puff of air. Moth’s light blinked once, a gentle nudge to keep going.

Moth then led Saffy to some moon-white flowers. Their petals felt like soft velvet. Moth hovered above and her glow lit a dewdrop on a petal. The dewdrop was like a tiny mirror. It held the big round moon and all its gentle light.

Saffy looked into the dewdrop. She watched the moon shimmer. And then a warm thought opened in her mind, like a flower turning to the sun. Her lullaby was not lost. It was only sleeping. It was tucked away inside her, the way the flowers slept under the moon, waiting to be woken softly.

Moth seemed to understand. She guided Saffy closer to the sleeping blossoms. Her warm light leaned toward them as if it were asking them to sing. It whispered of moonlight and rest. Then a sound, faint as a sigh on a warm evening, drifted from the flowers. It was a melody, sweet and soft and peaceful, like a whisper of dreams.

It was her lullaby. Saffy’s heart felt warm and full, like a little nest ready for a sleepy bird. She hummed along. Her voice joined the gentle tune. Moth’s light pulsed, happy and warm, in the quiet night.

“Thank you, Moth,” Saffy whispered. A happy little yawn stretched her nose toward the moon. Moth’s light seemed to nod. Together they went back to Saffy’s cozy clover bed. The lullaby was a gentle song in Saffy’s heart now, clear and comforting. She snuggled down. Her eyes felt heavy and warm. She pulled the clover leaves closer, like a soft blanket. The moonlight made soft patterns on the ground. Saffy felt perfectly safe and snug, wrapped in the quiet peace of the night. And soon, with the gentle light of Moth and the sweet clear memory of her lullaby singing softly in her heart, Saffy drifted off to sleep. Her dreams were full of moonlit melodies and the quiet comfort of a true friend. Everything was just right.
